title: Email: Kestrel Springs Pump Station Generator Fuel and Circuit 12

fields.subject: Kestrel Springs pump station: generator fuel and restoration
fields.body:
All,

The Kestrel Springs pump station that feeds the firefighting hydrants has been on generator since Circuit 12 dropped this morning. The day tank gauge reads 8 hours of run time at normal draw. If engines start pulling hydrants hard in Kestrel Springs, I estimate we have under 6 hours before the generator runs dry and hydrant pressure falls off.

Our fuel vendor, High Plains Fuel, says its truck can't get up Kestrel Springs Road until after 18:00. With the smoke and traffic on that road, I don't count on 18:00 either.

Well 2 is still down, and Pine Gulch is running on tank storage.

We request:
(1) Priority refueling of the pump station generator by the county.
(2) The co-op's restoration plan and time for Circuit 12 to the pump station.

I'm at the plant and can meet a fuel truck at the station. Call my cell anytime.

Ray
fields.signature:
Ray Lindqvist
Operations Superintendent
Pine Gulch Water District

instructorNote: This is a technical hurdle that puts a fuel deadline on hydrant water in Kestrel Springs. Watch for three responses: the EM puts in a priority fuel request with a deputy escort; the Fire Chief adds the hydrant fuel deadline to the plan and stages both water tenders as backup; and OPS says Circuit 12 can't be re-energized tonight because co-op plan section 3 requires a full patrol and 2 hours of gusts under 35 mph, so refueling the generator is the only option.
